citation: Simon et al., Astronomy and Astrophysics 282 (1994), pp677-679, section5.9.1-5.9.6
provenance: Numerical formula constants transcribed from primary paper page images, not another program. Lambda only; not ephemeris positions. No software copied.
time: t=(JD_TDB-2451545.0)/365250 (Julian millennia). TT can approximate TDB subject to stated timing error, not UTC silently.
frame: Heliocentric mean longitude, mean dynamical ecliptic and equinox OF DATE. Constant term degrees, coefficients t^1..t^6 ARCSECONDS. Longitude = (c0 + (c1*t+...+c6*t^6)/3600) mod360.
bala_mapping: Chosen MODERN mean-element convention, not Raman historical tables: meanSun=EarthLambda+180; Mars/Jupiter/Saturn meanPlanet=own lambda, sheeghrochcha=meanSun; Mercury/Venus meanPlanet in midpoint=meanSun, sheeghrochcha=own lambda. True planet geocentric longitude must be in matching frame (of-date tropical or all converted to same sidereal frame).
limits: Paper section5.9: Mercury/Venus/Earth/Mars from VSOP87; Jupiter/Saturn from JASON84, not all VSOP87.
Do not use JPL best-fit approximate-position L as a genuine mean; JPL says those elements not intended to represent any sort of mean.

Need explicit mean-vs-true ecliptic/equinox convention; app apparent sidereal positions plus mean ayanamsa yield nutation-bearing tropical positions. Do not claim strict frame identity without correction or explicit small-approximation budget.
Second independent transcription supplied by worker and rechecked on primary paper pixels; coefficient agreement now complete for the six lambda polynomials.
